At PMY Group, we are proud to be working with more than 1,000 valued clients in 15 countries. We have built a team of more than 500 talented professionals with more than 40 years of combined industry experience.
POSITION OVERVIEW

As a Client Facing Data Analyst, you will play a crucial role in enabling data-driven decision-making by transforming, analyzing, and reporting with a variety of data across performance, commercial and operational systems. This role is ideal for a detail-oriented professional with a strong analytical mindset who thrives in a collaborative, data-rich environment. You will design, develop, and maintain dashboards and reports to monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) and other essential metrics, providing clients and business leaders with insights that inform strategic decisions. As a member of our tech-forward team, you will continuously adapt and integrate cloud native AI solutions and tools to improve data quality and advance client goals. Your ability to translate complex data into clear, actionable insights will be instrumental in advancing client objectives and delivering measurable value.

This role is an individual contributor position with opportunities for growth into senior analytics roles.

RESPONSIBILITIES

Data Collection and Analysis

Collect, analyze, and report data from various sources, ensuring comprehensive and accurate insights.
Perform regular data quality checks to ensure accuracy and integrity across data sources.
Identify trends, patterns, and anomalies in data to derive actionable insights that support strategic decision-making.
Use natural language AI tools for ad hoc data exploration to accelerate discovery and guide areas of inquiry.

Dashboard and Reporting Development

Design, develop, and maintain dashboards and reports to monitor KPIs and other essential metrics.
Present data findings and insights to clients and stakeholders in a clear, concise, and impactful manner.
Create dashboard and reporting proofs of concept where appropriate with natural language AI tools (e.g. Google Gemini in Looker / Amazon Q in QuickSight).

Client Engagement and KPI Development

Guide clients in verbalizing their business goals and assist them in establishing KPIs to measure progress toward those goals.
Proactively manage the iteration of these goals and metrics as you build trusted client relationships.

Analytics Ownership and Insight

Own analytics outputs end-to-end, from data validation and dashboard development through insight generation and stakeholder delivery.
Take accountability for the accuracy, relevance, and adoption of analytics products, ensuring insights are clearly communicated and actionable for both client and internal stakeholders.
Proactively identify opportunities to improve reporting, refine KPIs, and surface recommendations that support operational and strategic decision-making.
Collaborate with engineering on cutting edge approaches to provide clients with access to agents trained on their data (Google BigQuery Agent Analytics, Amazon Redshift/Bedrock/Q, Azure Synapse/ML).

Cross-Functional Collaboration

Collaborate with cross-functional teams to identify data needs and provide analytical support aligned with project goals.
Experience working with clients and in-house teams across different time zones is highly desirable.

Strategy and Process Improvement

Contribute to the development and implementation of data-driven strategies and initiatives across multiple projects.
Contribute to project improvement methodologies, benchmarking and change management practices to enhance project outcomes.

Additional Responsibilities

Perform additional duties assigned to support evolving business needs.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS & EXPERIENCE

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required or preferred. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
4–6 years of experience in a data analyst, business intelligence, or analytics-focused role with a strong track record in data analysis and reporting.
Bachelor’s degree in Business, Data & Analytics, Information Systems, or a related field.
Prior experience in sports, live events & entertainment, or consulting is preferred.
Proficiency with data visualization tools such as Power BI, Tableau, or Looker, and strong SQL skills for data extraction, transformation, and analysis.
Experience working with relational and analytical databases such as PostgreSQL, MySQL, BigQuery, Redshift, or Snowflake.
Comfort working end-to-end with data, including writing and optimizing SQL queries, validating datasets, and translating outputs into business-ready insights.
Familiarity with cloud analytics platforms and tooling across AWS, Google Cloud Platform, or Azure.
Ability to leverage AI-assisted analytics capabilities across cloud platforms for data preparation, validation, and analysis, with familiarity in AI-enabled SQL functions and emerging ML tools such as BigQuery ML, AWS SageMaker, or Azure Synapse/ML.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with high attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple priorities.
Exceptional verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to present insights to both technical and non-technical audiences.
Demonstrated initiative, ownership, and accountability in delivering high-quality analytics work.
Familiarity with data privacy and data governance practices is a plus.

Impact

HDR is looking for an Environmental Scientist 1 to support utility clients with environmental and construction permitting and compliance. This role has a primary focus on construction stormwater management permitting and compliance, with supplemental work supporting floodplain development permitting, wetland permitting, right-of-way permitting, local planning approvals, and wildlife compliance support.
In this role, the candidate would be expected to:
- Supporting ongoing project compliance through construction (reviewing inspection reports, attending routine calls, post-construction site visits and documentation).
- Accommodating changing project schedules and scopes – shifting attention as needed.
- Managing tasks between competing project interests; tracking workload with support of supervisor.
- Effectively communicate over phone, email, or messaging platforms.
- Review local, State, and Federal regulations for applicability to projects
- Perform pre-construction and post-construction site visits
- Review engineering design packages for environmental / local permitting compliance
- Develop permitting matrices and timelines – for integration into client templates or overall schedules
The candidate would work with an experienced team including other environmental scientists and project managers of varying experience and backgrounds. Candidate responsibilities would evolve to include:
- Coordinating directly with client and permitting approval agencies representing HDR
- Directing internal resources/supporting staff (CAD/GIS, wildlife biologists, land agents, public outreach)- Coordinating/attending field visits
- Overseeing deliverable production
- Review deliverables for consistency with client project scope

- Managing deliverable production and distribution- Upload and track permitting submittals through jurisdictional permitting portals
- Conduct file management per client and internal specifications

- Development of figures and map sets in coordination with GIS/CAD staff
Preferred Qualifications
- Minimum 2 years of experience.
- Experience in Bluebeam, GIS or CAD drafting.
- Experience in local or federal permitting or agency review processes.
- Strong technical writing skills, including experience preparing technical reports, agency correspondence, permit applications, and other project documentation.
- Experience on active construction sites.
- Strong organizational skills and ability to work in an environment with changing deadlines and priorities.
- Ability to understand hydrology across disturbed landscape, read topographic maps, and visualize erosion and sediment transport.
- Self-motivated, able to work independently and as part of a team.
- Ability to safely drive around the State either in personal car or Company rental is a must. A valid Colorado driver’s license is required.
Our team understands the value of expanding individual work portfolios and experience to keep job duties interesting and achieve career sustainability and growth. Additional workload and type would depend on skills, experience, and interest. A comfort and enthusiasm interacting with a variety of individuals will help foster successful career growth.
Team members are currently working from Fort Collins, Denver, and remote locations along the front range and western slope of Colorado. The preferred candidate will be based out of the Fort Collins office. Flexibility on number of days in the office and working remotely is expected, with the assumption that the candidate would be in office 2-3 days per week to facilitate training and skill development. Long-term remote vs in office time is negotiable and will be based on past experience and level of training required. Our team encourages a healthy work-life balance that focuses on quality of service to our clients and participation in recurrent meetings while allowing for flexibility in work schedules. Site visits are sporadic with limited/few visits during winter months and up to 2-3 visits per month during busier months. Site visits rarely require overnight stay.

Organization Description: 

Colorado Food Cluster (CFC) Inc. partners with community organizations throughout Colorado to provide critical support, resources and services to students and their families. Through culturally responsive approaches, CFC provides nutritious meals to children and families throughout Colorado leveraging federally funded programs. CFC continuously seeks opportunities and programs that remove barriers to access food, for all people in our communities using innovative solutions to improve access to nutritious food.

Job Overview:

The Program Coordinator will support the successful implementation of the Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP) and Summer Food Service Program (SFSP), ensuring CFC meets applicable federal and state requirements as a Sponsor organization. The Coordinator will  support program implementation, day-to-day operations, and continued development of CFC’s newest Medicaid meal delivery program.

The Program Coordinator will manage a variety of daily administrative and program responsibilities, including recordkeeping, partner onboarding and support, site visits, program audits, service expansion, and communications. The Program Coordinator will work closely with partners to ensure they have the information and resources needed to successfully provide services while meeting required program timelines and deadlines.

The Program Coordinator must be able to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment and support CFC programs as needs evolve throughout the year. Travel to different regions of Colorado will be required.

This position includes a 30-day introductory period, after which the employee becomes eligible for health insurance benefits.

Essential Duties/Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

Support planning and coordination of ongoing programs and activities for CACFP, Home Delivered Meals through Medicaid, and SFSP.
Proactively and independently manage assigned daily tasks, projects, and program deadlines.
Maintain an understanding of rules, regulations, and policies applicable to Federal Nutrition Programs, stay current on updated requirements, and interpret operational impacts.
Design systems and structures for effective program implementation and expansion efforts for CACFP, Medicaid, and SFSP.
Support monthly CACFP and SFSP claim preparation, including review and reconciliation of attendance, meal counts, enrollment records, Income Eligibility Forms, menus, production records, and other required documentation.
Identify missing, incomplete, expired, or noncompliant documentation and communicate necessary corrections to participating sites prior to claim submission.
Track claim deadlines and required program submissions to ensure timely and accurate reporting.
Support preparation and organization of program records for state reviews, audits, and other oversight activities.
Conduct required federal onsite monitoring visits to providers and caretakers across Colorado, including but not limited to home care providers, afterschool programs, and childcare centers.
Document monitoring findings and communicate required follow-up or corrective actions to participating sites when applicable.
Coordinate with food vendors regarding menus, meal orders, delivery schedules, substitutions, documentation, service issues, and program compliance.
Train and onboard new centers, home providers, vendors, and other partners on CFC processes, documentation requirements, program systems, meal service procedures, and applicable program requirements.
Maintain consistent follow-up with partners regarding outstanding documentation, deadlines, compliance issues, and operational changes.
Engage partners to inform them of program offerings and enroll students, centers, and home providers in meal delivery programs.
Work with community organizations to inform them about programming and support enrollment efforts.
Identify and manage partners with aligned missions and priorities.
Manage daily email and phone communications in the CRM system from families accessing programming.
Support families with program registration platforms and troubleshoot issues.
Develop and disseminate high-quality communications to support program implementation and expansion.
Facilitate external presentations about CFC programs for multiple audiences.
Support development and distribution of external communications, including but not limited to newsletters, social media, and customer service communications.
Other duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications and Experiences: 

Bachelor's degree or relevant years of experience. 
Registered Dietitian or Certified Nutritionist credential required to support Medicaid program requirements.
2+ of experience working with communities. 
Excellent organizational and time management skills.
Detail-oriented and efficient.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Strong attention to detail and demonstrated ability to review documentation for accuracy and completeness.
Ability to communicate expectations, deadlines, and compliance concerns professionally with external partners.
Ability to execute projects from development phase to operation.
Experience implementing public programming preferably programs funded through federal funds.
Ability to work independently in a remote work environment while maintaining consistent communication, documentation, and accountability.
Ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines while maintaining accurate and organized records.
Have access to reliable transportation.
Have a valid drivers license.
Ability to travel to all areas of Colorado as needed.

Candidates who are bilingual are strongly encouraged to apply.
Focus and special interest in food insecurity, childcare and policy.
Experience with CACFP, SFSP, Medicaid, or other federal/state nutrition or human services programs. 
Proficiency working in Google Suite.
Problem Solver.

Our mission is to implement federal and state regulations to protect human health and the environment while allowing the environmentally sound operations of industrial, agricultural, commercial, and governmental activities vital to a prosperous economy. We issue air, water, and solid and hazardous waste permits that restrict discharges to environmentally safe levels. Staff members inspect and monitor regulated entities; provide compliance and technical assistance; monitor and assess air, land, and water quality; use enforcement actions as necessary to ensure compliance; and respond to incidents involving spills to soil or waters of the state.

The Geologist 2 serves as a technical specialist within the Geological Services Section, providing advanced geological expertise to support IDEM’s mission of protecting human health and the environment. Strong analytical and critical thinking abilities.
Proficiency interpreting complex geological, hydrogeologic, and environmental data.
Effective written and verbal communication skills across technical and non technical audiences.
Ability to work independently while contributing collaboratively within program teams.
High attention to detail and accuracy in technical work products.
Understanding of environmental regulations related to site investigation and cleanup activities.

A Day In The Life

Evaluate and assist in developing geologically related plans and documents.

Position summary

The Solutions Engineer designs the operation.

When a customer needs receiving, storage, picking and shipping to work as one operation rather than as separate pieces of equipment, the Solutions Engineer analyzes their data, maps the process, designs the material flow across every functional area, and produces the concept everything downstream is built from.

The work is industrial engineering applied to a commercial pursuit: order profiles, rates, capacity, labor, and the tradeoffs between them, worked out with the customer and defensible in front of them. The Solutions Engineer hands the Application Engineer a high-level layout with the flow and the rates behind it, and the Application Engineer makes it real.

Staffing test: are we designing the operation, or equipping one that is already defined? A Solutions Engineer engages on greenfield facilities, material flow across multiple functional areas, reconfiguration or process redesign, and any pursuit with customer operational data to analyze. Replacements, expansions, defined-scope RFP responses and repeat scope run without one, and that is the normal case.

Character Qualifications

Innovation – We create a culture of relentless improvement of solutions and processes to make every day better.

Integrity – We are open, honest, and committed to giving the straight story every time.

Service – We serve our clients, families, communities, and most importantly our people who are empowered and safe in making decisions and taking actions that dare to make us better.

Ownership – We take full, personal, individual responsibility for our actions and our work.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

Intake & qualification

Give the technical feasibility read on bid/no-bid. The commercial decision sits above this department.

Solution development

Analyze the customer’s data directly: order profiles, SKU velocity and slotting, volume and seasonality, labor and rate modeling. Establish the rate and capacity basis the solution is sized from.
Map the process across every functional area in scope and design the material flow that ties them into one operation: routes, buffers, decision points and interfaces.
Produce the block-level layout by functional area and select the technology class for each.
Select the third-party partners in the solution where our own product is not the answer. Commodity scope stays generic and goes to execution.
Evaluate technology feasibility and weigh the tradeoffs between options: cost, throughput, flexibility, footprint and lifecycle.

Customer & supply

Serve as the primary technical liaison to the customer through the pursuit, presenting and defending the concept and the tradeoffs behind it.

Execution & turnover

○Reviewing the RFP, contract and statement of work for risk

Throughput, capacity and queuing analysis. Applied statistics on operational data. Geometry and trigonometry applied to facility layout. Reasoning. Our mission is to implement federal and state regulations to protect human health and the environment while allowing the environmentally sound operations of industrial, agricultural, commercial, and governmental activities vital to a prosperous economy. We issue air, water, and solid and hazardous waste permits that restrict discharges to environmentally safe levels. Staff members inspect and monitor regulated entities; provide compliance and technical assistance; monitor and assess air, land, and water quality; use enforcement actions as necessary to ensure compliance; and respond to incidents involving spills to soil or waters of the state.

Role Overview

The Geologist 2 serves as a technical specialist within the Geological Services Section, providing advanced geological expertise to support IDEM’s mission of protecting human health and the environment. This position assists in the characterization and remediation of uncontrolled waste and spill sites by performing and evaluating complex geological, environmental, engineering, and hydrogeologic work. The Geologist 2 supports regulatory decision‑making and contributes to restoring contaminated properties to safe and productive use.

Core Competencies

Strong analytical and critical thinking abilities.
Proficiency interpreting complex geological, hydrogeologic, and environmental data.
Effective written and verbal communication skills across technical and non technical audiences.
Ability to work independently while contributing collaboratively within program teams.
High attention to detail and accuracy in technical work products.
Understanding of environmental regulations related to site investigation and cleanup activities.

Minimum Requirements

Bachelor's degree in geology or a related geoscience field.
Relevant professional experience in geology, hydrogeology, environmental geology, or related work.
Valid Indiana driver's license.

Preferred Qualifications

Master's degree in geology, hydrogeology, or environmental science.
Is an Indiana Licensed Professional Geologist (LPG).
Experience working with contaminated site assessments, remediation projects, or regulatory programs.
Familiarity with IDEM guidance, OLQ procedures, and state/federal environmental regulations.
Experience using GIS tools, geological modeling software, or environmental data analysis platforms.

Salary

to view the total compensation package.

A Day In The Life

The essential functions of this role are as follows:

Provide geologic consultation utilizing technical expertise regarding engineering geology, hydrogeology, and geology.
Understand, interpret, and employ applicable State and Federal regulatory rules, guidance, and policies related to geological investigations and contaminant remediation.
Lead or assist field teams during site investigations.
Evaluate and assist in developing geologically related plans and documents.
Develop and write technical reports and correspondence including tabulating and interpreting data for reports.
Follow proper sampling procedures and use appropriate geophysical and other field techniques.
Review and evaluate technical guidance documents, reports, journals, and related articles.
Determine historic geologic and hydrogeologic conditions utilizing agency files.
Assist in geological enforcement actions.
Provide technical assistance to other staff, state and federal agencies, industries, contractors, and the public.

These additional duties may be performed if this position is at the Indiana Department of Natural Resources (DNR)

Perform complex data analysis and interpretation to determine locations and extent of underground sources of drinking water.

These additional duties may be performed if this position is at the Indiana Department of Transportation (INDOT)

Work with the Testing Team to report findings and make recommendations of construction material aggregates and soils for highway construction. Research/investigate into construction contracts that do not comply with specifications.
Administer INDOT’s Certified Aggregate Producers Program (CAPP) program at the District level. Regulate and monitor all aggregate sources assigned to the District and ensure compliance with Department specifications and guidelines.

Licensed Professional Geologist in Indiana preferred.
Extensive knowledge of the principles, practices, theories, and methodologies applied to geologic/hydrogeologic science and related fields.
Thorough knowledge of and the ability to interpret and apply all applicable federal and state laws, environmental regulations, acts, and guidelines.
Extensive knowledge of applied statistics, environmental design, geologic sampling, and interpretation of geologic analysis.
Thorough knowledge of remedial and corrective action as it relates to various program areas.
Ability to conduct intensive research for geologic and hydrogeological advancement of the program area.
Ability to determine resolutions and new approaches to various geotechnical problems.
Specialized knowledge of geophysical instrumentation including Electro magnetometer, Resistivity Meter, and Seismograph.
Specialized knowledge of well hydraulics, ground water modeling, drinking water management, waste and wastewater management, and related regulations.

new_jobs.description:
Position summary

The Solutions Engineer designs the operation.

When a customer needs receiving, storage, picking and shipping to work as one operation rather than as separate pieces of equipment, the Solutions Engineer analyzes their data, maps the process, designs the material flow across every functional area, and produces the concept everything downstream is built from.

The work is industrial engineering applied to a commercial pursuit: order profiles, rates, capacity, labor, and the tradeoffs between them, worked out with the customer and defensible in front of them. The Solutions Engineer hands the Application Engineer a high-level layout with the flow and the rates behind it, and the Application Engineer makes it real.

Staffing test: are we designing the operation, or equipping one that is already defined? A Solutions Engineer engages on greenfield facilities, material flow across multiple functional areas, reconfiguration or process redesign, and any pursuit with customer operational data to analyze. Replacements, expansions, defined-scope RFP responses and repeat scope run without one, and that is the normal case.

Character Qualifications

Innovation – We create a culture of relentless improvement of solutions and processes to make every day better.

Integrity – We are open, honest, and committed to giving the straight story every time.

Service – We serve our clients, families, communities, and most importantly our people who are empowered and safe in making decisions and taking actions that dare to make us better.

Ownership – We take full, personal, individual responsibility for our actions and our work.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

Intake & qualification

Give the technical feasibility read on bid/no-bid. The commercial decision sits above this department.

Solution development

Analyze the customer’s data directly: order profiles, SKU velocity and slotting, volume and seasonality, labor and rate modeling. Establish the rate and capacity basis the solution is sized from.
Map the process across every functional area in scope and design the material flow that ties them into one operation: routes, buffers, decision points and interfaces.
Produce the block-level layout by functional area and select the technology class for each.
Select the third-party partners in the solution where our own product is not the answer. Commodity scope stays generic and goes to execution.
Evaluate technology feasibility and weigh the tradeoffs between options: cost, throughput, flexibility, footprint and lifecycle.

Customer & supply

Work in front of the customer alongside Sales as the technical voice on the solution.
Serve as the primary technical liaison to the customer through the pursuit, presenting and defending the concept and the tradeoffs behind it.

Execution & turnover

Hand execution a package they can build from: the reasoning and assumptions, not only the drawings.
Support the Project Manager through the early phases of execution.

Contributes to

○Reviewing the RFP, contract and statement of work for risk

○Protecting the project budget and gross margin

○Applying Fives equipment and configurations to the requirement

○Layout drawings

○Electrical and controls architecture

○The mechanical estimate

○CRD authorship

○Technical writing, description of operation and scope

○Specification compliance and acceptance criteria

○Bid strategy

○Risk assessment

○Vendor and subcontractor evaluation

○The technical basis for acceptance criteria and test procedures

○The standardization program and product classification

Working with the rest of the team

Partner They bring You keep Application Engineer Equipment selection, detailed layout, manifest, BOM, CRD and the estimate The flow, the rates, the block layout, and the technology in it Electrical Estimating Engineer Controls architecture and the electrical estimate The operational flow and decision points their controls serve Principal Solutions Engineer Cross-discipline design review and final technical authority The concept on your pursuit Offering Manager Proposal schedule, bid strategy, workload prioritization, and who staffs each subsystem The technical concept and its defensibility Sales Commercial strategy, the customer relationship, the bid/no-bid decision The technical read and the operation the customer is buying Operations / Project Management Acceptance criteria, field execution, commodity equipment selection The technical basis the criteria are built on

Qualifications

Education and experience

Bachelor’s degree in Industrial Engineering preferred. Engineering or an equivalent combination of education and experience considered.
8 to 12 years designing automated material handling or distribution operations.
Required: ownership of facility-level or operation-level concepts spanning multiple functional areas.
Required: hands-on analysis of customer operational data, including order profiles, velocity, volumes and seasonality, and the rate and capacity modeling built on it.
Required: direct customer-facing technical experience during a sales pursuit.
Preferred, not required: material handling, distribution, parcel or baggage experience, and familiarity with AS/RS, goods-to-person, robotics and sortation technologies. Candidates from adjacent automation industries are expressly welcome.
Familiarity with discrete-event simulation, sufficient to commission and interpret it. Building the models is not required.
Excel to a high standard. SQL, Power BI or equivalent an advantage. Block-level layout in SketchUp or AutoCAD.

Skills

Language. Reads and interprets customer specifications, operational data, contracts and statements of work. Presents and defends concepts to customers and to senior management. Mathematical. Throughput, capacity and queuing analysis. Applied statistics on operational data. Geometry and trigonometry applied to facility layout. Reasoning. Defines problems, collects data, establishes facts, and draws valid conclusions from incomplete information, stating the assumptions used to get there.

Travel

Travel to customer sites, vendor plants and job sites, typically 25% to 40%. Occasional international travel for site visits or training.

Progression

The Solutions Engineer role has four levels: Junior Solutions Engineer, Solutions Engineer, Senior Solutions Engineer and Principal Solutions Engineer. Senior comes from consistently sound operation design and passing the discipline’s method review, and carries sign-off on others’ concepts along with coaching. Principal holds cross-discipline technical authority. None of these levels manages people. Line management is a separate route, through Supervisor, Manager and Director of Solutions, open by choice rather than by seniority.
